enquiry: We produce an opaque, concentrated milk product that flows through a processing line. We currently sample it for fat and protein analysis and would like earlier information about composition changes. Product temperature and texture vary during production. We want an initial spectroscopy concept and a practical comparison experiment, while retaining our laboratory checks.

items.finding: The text notes that the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands represents a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solutions in NIR and MIR, requiring tempered sample holders.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests that temperature fluctuations in the flowing milk product could impact the spectral baseline, meaning temperature compensation or sample conditioning should be tested.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This finding refers to biopharmaceutical downstream processing and general aqueous solutions rather than an opaque flowing milk product in an in-line system.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
